Story Summary: Fixed an off-by-one bug in a C++ loop that skipped the last array element when summing grades. Matches the small fix of correcting a clothing size label that displayed the wrong value to shoppers.
Changed button colors and label text on the game menu after teammate feedback. Comparable to renaming a try-on screen button to 'Try It On' because testers found the wording confusing.
Updated a typo and a broken link in a company web page footer after a customer reported it. Similar in size to correcting a broken help link in the app.
Wrote a function that validated user input, rejecting negative numbers and non-numeric text, and reprompted the user. Comparable to validating a height or weight entry field in a profile.
Added a delete operation to a linked list with a few unit tests. Similar in effort to letting a user remove one saved item from a wishlist.
Added a simple settings toggle for sound effects that saved to a local file. Comparable to saving a light or dark mode preference in the app.

Implemented a stack-based expression evaluator with parentheses handling and error messages. Similar in complexity to a size-conversion calculator, since shoppers report that brand sizing is inconsistent (TrueFit).

Built a command-line calculator parser supporting operator precedence and basic error reporting. Comparable to building a size-chart lookup that converts a shopper's measurements into the matching size for each brand, since sizes vary widely between brands.
Created a scoreboard screen showing win totals pulled from a save file with sorting. Similar to a favorites list that displays saved outfits sorted by date.
Built a filterable table in a React dashboard with search and dropdown filters. Comparable to a catalog screen letting shoppers filter garments by size, color, and price.
Implemented a binary search tree with insert, search, delete, and traversal, plus unit tests. Similar in effort to organizing a garment catalog for fast lookup by category.

Implemented game save and load using file serialization, handling corrupt files gracefully. Comparable to saving a user's body measurements and favorite outfits between app sessions so they never re-enter them.
Designed a small relational database with three tables and wrote the queries behind a reporting page. Comparable to storing user profiles, garments, and saved outfits.
Integrated a third-party REST API for address lookup, including error handling and retries. Similar to pulling product data and prices from a retailer's catalog API.
Built a login system with hashed passwords, session handling, and a password reset flow. Comparable to account creation for the app, where users want body data kept private.
Developed a multi-screen mobile prototype with navigation, shared state, and data persistence over two weeks. Similar to the browse, select, and try-on flow of the app.
Deployed a web service to the cloud with a database, environment configuration, and automated tests running on each commit. Comparable to hosting the garment catalog and user accounts.

Implemented computer-controlled opponent logic with several difficulty levels and testing across many game states. Similar in uncertainty to tuning fit recommendations that must work across varied body types.
Built a real-time camera feature with live video, overlays, and permission handling. Similar to showing a garment over the live camera view, which is the core of the app.
Wrote a full graph pathfinding program with a custom data structure, file input, visualization, and extensive tests. Comparable to aligning a 3D garment to detected body landmarks.
Implemented a payment checkout flow with a third-party provider, order records, receipts, and failure handling. Comparable to a buy-now flow linking to retailers after a user tries on a garment.

Attempted a realistic physics-based cloth simulation that drapes and stretches to a user's measured body. Too large and unclear to estimate, as research found AR fit is weakest at bust, waist, and length (Iowa State study).
